pillar_reactions.evidence: Engaged substantively rather than just agreeing, and redirected the pillar toward his own needs: 'I'm just concerned with ability basically and the imbalances I have like that I have flat feet... when I was a baby I had to wear a brace on both legs.' He then framed what he actually wants: 'I would want to approach this with some level of like a physical therapy, like, mindset, not that it's physical therapy, but like the mobility drills that you're talking about... and to kind of slowly start correcting things.' The rep answered with the weak-points targeting and pushed back usefully on stretching-versus-strengthening. As a certified yoga teacher he was the most technically literate audience for this pillar in the batch.

No pushback and no questions. The rep validated the inputs — organic cooking, no seed oils, whole foods, extra virgin olive oil — and correctly named the two live problems the prospect had already identified himself: portion size and timing. The prospect volunteered the digestion issue that complicates it: 'I do get bloated a lot when I eat... it's difficult for me to say, all right, I just had a large enough meal to get all this protein, and then to time it right with the workout.' He also confirmed the eating window and fasted training already suit him. The rep's guess that protein intake is short went unchallenged but also unverified.

Agreed and tied it to his stated goal — 'that's my goal. I want this to be a lifestyle kind of integration.' He had pre-sold himself on this pillar much earlier, when asked what was missing from an already substantial routine: 'a personalized approach, a degree of community, accountability, some constructive criticism, feedback, whatever, insight' and 'there's a certain degree where I would benefit from just like, this is the plan, you follow the plan, it works.' Given decision fatigue is his named daily problem, the take-the-decisions-off-you angle was the strongest available and the rep used it: 'that's someone. It takes this load off your shoulder, at least in one area of your life.'

anchors.raw: there was a point in my life where when I was a lot younger, I lost like 80 pounds and I kept it off for like five or six years and it, you know, it was not, not an issue.
anchors.note: He has already solved this problem once, alone and for free, and sustained it for five or six years. The strongest available argument for not paying $6,000, and it went entirely unaddressed. The counter is sitting in his own words — that he was younger, and that his life then was not what it is now — and the rep never drew it out.

anchors.raw: I'm going to a dry hot sauna, five or six days per week for 20 to 25 minutes per session. I'm doing an hour of yoga six days a week... I meditate twice a day for about 20 minutes.
anchors.note: An enormous existing time and money commitment to self-care already in place — sauna sessions, a residential yoga certification, daily practice, tai chi, supplements including whey, collagen and creatine. This is not a buyer who needs convincing that structured investment in health is worthwhile, which is why the rep's what's-missing question worked so well. Effort is not the constraint; recovery and money are.

anchors.raw: if you really want to work with him for longer, and we had guys that they wanted to go for a year, for example, yeah, that is possible... That will cost you another $3,000, and that's it. You don't need to pay another $6,000.
anchors.note: The most commercially significant disclosure in this batch. A second six months costs $3,000 — half rate — and it was volunteered unprompted in response to a question about what happens after month six. Critically, $3,000 for six months is exactly the price quoted as an INITIAL price to Bennu Kham Ra Ankh Aten four days earlier, which raises the possibility that the renewal rate is being used as a discount on new business. Once a buyer knows the second six months is half price, the first six months has to justify a 2x premium on the same service.

anchors.raw: I have people that owe me money that are in the process of paying me... I'm in the process of paying for repairs on the roof and the siding and the landscaping and the driveway and the plumbing. So I just have like massive amounts of money that's like in and out.
anchors.competitor: Estate carrying costs and pre-sale repairs
anchors.note: Not an affordability objection — he says outright 'I don't have a problem with the amount' — but genuine and externally dependent illiquidity. The September date rests on third parties catching up on contracted payments and on a house sale completing, neither of which he controls, which makes the seven-week follow-up materially riskier than it sounds.

unmet_demand.want: A physical-therapy-minded approach to a congenital lower-limb alignment issue, an uneven gait and flat feet — asked for explicitly
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He was braced on both legs for the first six months of life, walks unevenly, and says the imbalance compounds if he walks too far or raises the incline. The rep answered with weak-point mobility protocols and a strengthening argument, which may well be right, but there is no clinician in the offer and nobody assessed the gait. He asked for something adjacent to physical therapy and is being sold coaching that is not it.

unmet_demand.want: Help with recovery when sleep is broken by circumstance rather than by habit — he asked directly what to do when he is awake at 3am and due to train at 6
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep gave a reasonable answer at the very end — do something, keep it light, not heavy — but the underlying problem is a chronic stress state that no training programme addresses, and he had already ruled out the standard sleep hygiene advice because he does all of it. The weekly check-in asks how he slept; nothing in the offer changes why he does not.

unmet_demand.want: Community and people on the same wavelength — named twice as part of what is missing, alongside his description of growing isolation
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The one-to-one product is a solo relationship with a coach. Primal University and its community were never mentioned on this call at all, despite being pitched or bundled on most others in this batch, and despite community being one of only four things he listed when asked what was missing. A relevant asset the company owns went unoffered.

unmet_demand.want: Support for the psychological load that is driving the physiology — the fight-or-flight state, the nightmares, the isolation
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme was positioned as part of the answer — 'this is going to be like a part of work on yourself too' — but contains no mental health component and no referral pathway, and none was suggested. He is buying a training programme partly as psychological repair, and the offer neither claims that nor disclaims it.
